## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The one change needed is to make `--exclude` read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, as the project's CLI flag policy requires. The filtering logic itself has test coverage for single patterns, multiple patterns and the end-to-end archive.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns, and it logs each skipped path. The pull request also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and `main` tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default `--exclude` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, `.log` files are still archived, because the flag uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, which is the case this rule exists for. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose a separator for multiple patterns and document it in `docs/flags.md`, then extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with a case where the variable is set.
